title: feat(auth): withdraw an authorized AI assistant, for the person and for a platform administrator
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao9RVHLeGV8ByfXSADPXFwJD)_

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Fixes #31048

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：新增两个撤回入口：用户撤回自己授权过的 AI 助手（`POST /api/v1/auth/authorized-clients/withdraw`），平台管理员替所管理的人撤回（`POST /api/v1/auth/admin/authorized-clients/withdraw`）；SDK 增加 `oauth.authorizedClients.withdraw()` / `withdrawForUser()`。
- **为什么改**：授权页承诺「您可以随时在账户设置中撤销访问权限」，控制台已能列出授权过的助手，但没有可调用的撤回入口；#30894 的撤回按钮等的就是它。
- **风险与回滚**：只新增路由，现有路由不变。撤回与 `/oauth2/revoke` 共用同一段撤销代码（删授权记录 + 该客户端的刷新令牌），助手的令牌在下一次 MCP 调用即被拒。别人的 id 和不存在的 id 回同一个 404，探不出 id 是否存在。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/authorized-clients-withdraw.ts`（`findConsentOf` 的归属判断）；`auth-plugin.ts` 里管理员入口先跑 `gateAdmin`。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/authorized-clients-read.real-plugin.test.ts -t 31048`，预期 6 条通过。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

Two ObjectStack mounts beside the authorized-clients reads, both keyed by the consent `id` the reads answer on every row:

| Route | Body | Who |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `POST /api/v1/auth/authorized-clients/withdraw` | `{ id }` | the signed-in person, their own grant only |
| `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/authorized-clients/withdraw` | `{ userId, id }` | a platform administrator, behind the same `gateAdmin` as `GET /admin/authorized-clients` |

A withdraw revokes the grant through `revokeMcpGrant` (`mcp-token-revocation.ts`), the function `/oauth2/revoke` already uses: the consent row, then the client's refresh family, all through better-auth's own storage adapter. `mcpConsentAdmits` refuses the token on its next MCP call, and because the refresh family goes too, a refresh token the client still holds can't come back if the person authorizes the same assistant again later. The write is credited to whoever withdrew (`runAttributedToUser`, attribution only).

- `auth-route-ledger.ts`: two `sdk` rows (`oauth.authorizedClients.withdraw` / `withdrawForUser`), and a `server-only` row for better-auth's `POST /oauth2/delete-consent` that records the measurement below and names the new door. The read row's note now names the withdraw as its key's consumer.
- `@objectstack/client`: `oauth.authorizedClients.withdraw(id)` and `withdrawForUser(userId, id)`, both answering `AuthorizedClientWithdrawal` (`{ id }`). The stale `list()` doc line that pointed at `/oauth2/delete-consent` is corrected.
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`: one bullet in *The security model* (no docs page listed the authorized-clients doors before; this is the page that covers OAuth assistants).
- Doc comments that named `/oauth2/delete-consent` as "the Console's withdraw" (`authorized-clients-read.ts`, `mcp-token-revocation.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`) now name the new module.

### Design choice: (b), an ObjectStack mount

Measured on `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.12 (`deleteConsentEndpoint`): the vendor route does check ownership (`consent.userId !== session.user.id` → `UNAUTHORIZED`), so option (a) is not a security defect and nothing went to security#1. But it answers an unknown id `404 not_found` and another person's id `401 UNAUTHORIZED`, so a caller can tell them apart; it reads the row by id alone, and it deletes only the consent row, leaving the refresh family. Ledgering it as `sdk` would have pinned a two-answer, probe-able door with a 401 that means "not yours" rather than "not signed in". The mount gives one closed answer set:

| Caller → door | Unknown id | Another person's id | Own id |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| member → own | `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` (same bytes; row stays) | `200 { id }` |
| platform admin → own | `404` | `404` (same bytes; the own door is keyed by the session) | `200` |
| platform admin → admin `{userId, id}` | `404` (consent message) | `404` (same bytes when `id` isn't `userId`'s; row stays) | `200` |
| platform admin → admin, `userId` naming no user | `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with the admin read's message | | |
| member / org owner / org admin / the person → admin | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` | `403` (same bytes, also for `{}`) | `403` |
| anonymous → either | `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` | `401` | `401` |

Shape refusals on both doors: a query parameter, a foreign body key, a missing, blank or non-string `id`/`userId`, a non-object body → `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; JSON declared and unparseable → `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (`readJsonRequestBody`). A held session on the own door → `403` with the posture's own code. All codes come from the existing catalog; no spec key or error code is added.

### Audit

The grant and the revoke paths write no explicit `sys_audit_log` row. Both go through better-auth's adapter into the engine, and `sys_oauth_consent` is not in plugin-audit's `SKIP_OBJECTS`, so the generic writer records the grant as `create` and the revoke as `delete`. The withdraw goes through the same adapter, so it gets the same generic `delete` row with no new action value. The dogfood pin measures both rows on the real stack with plugin-audit installed. The `delete` row is credited to whoever withdrew: the person on the own door, the administrator on the admin door (`user_id`). An own withdraw made from an impersonation session hands `runAttributedToUser` `{ id, impersonatedBy }`, read off the session as `gateAdmin` and the auth before-hook read it. The revoke's writes therefore carry the attribution-only `impersonated_by` beside the person.

## Tests

- `plugin-auth` `authorized-clients-read.real-plugin.test.ts` (the shared harness: real `AuthManager`, real better-auth, real `AuthPlugin` routes on Hono): six new cases in two `#31048` describes. They cover a member withdrawing their own grant (row and refresh family gone, that grant's MCP token refused, the person's other grants and tokens untouched, a second withdraw is the not-found answer); another person's id from a member and from a platform admin on the own door (byte-identical to an unknown id, row stays, token still admitted); the shape refusals; an admin withdrawing a managed person's grant (token refused, list shrinks); a mismatched `userId`/`id` and an unknown user; and the non-admin matrix (member, org owner, org admin, the person themself: one `403` for existing, missing and empty bodies; anonymous `401`; nothing moves). One more `#31048` describe (2 cases) reads the credited actor from inside the revoke. An impersonation session yields `{ userId, impersonatedBy }`. An ordinary session or a blank `impersonatedBy` yields `{ userId }` alone.
- `auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts`: the hand-written objectstack-sourced roster gains both routes, each proven absent from better-auth's live table.
- `client` `oauth-authorized-clients.test.ts`: URL, method and exact body of both withdraws, throw on `404`/`403`, return types.
- dogfood `authorized-client-withdraw.dogfood.test.ts` (new): over HTTP on the showcase stack with the MCP server and plugin-audit. It drives a real DCR, consent and code-exchange grant. Another member's withdraw is the same `404` as an unknown id and the assistant keeps working. The owner's withdraw makes `initialize` answer `401` and the refresh grant `400 invalid_grant`, with audit rows as described above. On the admin door a member gets `403`, and the admin's withdraw refuses the token. Its generic `delete` row is credited to the administrator, not the person.
- dogfood `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal` / `admin-platform-admin-standing`: the new admin route classified in both derived sweeps (`objectstack-gate`; `ADMITTED`), each with a payload that reaches the gate.

## Acceptance notes

- **Refresh family scope.** `revokeMcpGrant` deletes the client's refresh tokens for the person across organizations (keyed by client and user, as `/oauth2/revoke` already does), while the consent it deletes is the one organization's. If a person granted the same client in two organizations, withdrawing one makes the other organization's session re-authorize when its access token expires (its consent stays, so no new consent prompt). This keeps one owner for "revoke a grant"; narrowing the refresh delete to `reference_id` would change `/oauth2/revoke` too and isn't in this card. Tracked in #31076.
- `POST /oauth2/delete-consent` stays mounted by better-auth's catch-all, unchanged, now ledgered `server-only` with the measurement. Shadowing or refusing it is not in this card.
- The route-count prose in `admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`'s header (11 + 24 = 31) was already stale before this change and is left alone, as that header itself says.

